question: During the initial phase of the action, citizens and stakeholders have been complaining about the online platform not working properly and about a lack of transparency in the automated system for screening and rejecting eligible homes, with citizens not being given sufficient information about the reasons for the rejection and the possibility of an appeal.

The improper functioning of the platform and the unforeseen blanket exclusion of homes purchased in 2026 led to nine questions and petitions being submitted to the Hellenic Parliament, 430 citizens’ complaints being lodged, a petition being submitted to the Greek Ombudsman and an out-of-court notice.

The regional offices of the Technical Chamber of Greece (TEE) recently sent letters highlighting that the problems are ongoing and asking for corrections1. In view of the above, can the Commission answer the following: 1.

Will it look into whether the platform is applying the required screening procedure and will it ask the Greek authorities to inform each rejected applicant about which property was screened and the specific criteria that were not met?
Will it verify whether the platform is functioning in accordance with the published terms, EU law and the co-funded target, especially with regard to unoccupied properties purchased in 2026?

What corrective measures will be considered to compensate those who lost the chance to participate in the programme as a result of the platform not working properly and will a new deadline be granted to those who purchased a home that is currently being used as a main residence and who were wrongly rejected having not been given the chance to participate, due to the correction being made after the deadline?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (26.11.2026) Under shared management, support under the Cohesion Policy Funds is provided according to an approach of complementarity and partnership between the Commission and the Member States.

The design, selection and implementation of projects are the responsibility of the competent managing authorities in the Member States, provided they comply with the principles laid down in the programming documents and with applicable national and EU legislation.

Member States must also ensure that the management and control system governing the selection of the projects, the implementation and the controls, including eligibility verification and the handling of complaints for co-financed projects comply with national and EU rules.

In accordance with Articles 69 and 73 of Regulation (EU) 2021/10601, Member States must have in place effective arrangements for examining complaints and apply transparent selection criteria and procedures. The Implementation Guide2 for the "Renovation of the Residence" action, published by the Greek authorities sets out the appeal procedures.

The Greek authorities are responsible for ensuring that the eligibility checks are carried out in accordance with the applicable programme conditions, including on tax or ownership information, and that the eligibility criteria are consistent with the published conditions, as well as for addressing technical deficiencies and for determining whether extensions of deadlines to obtain an eligibility certificate are justified.
1 Regulation (EU) 2021/1060 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 24 June 2021 laying down

common provisions on the European Regional Development Fund, the European Social Fund Plus, the Cohesion Fund, the Just Transition Fund and the European Maritime, Fisheries and Aquaculture Fund and financial rules for those and for the Asylum, Migration and Integration Fund, the Internal Security Fund and the Instrument for Financial Support for Border Management and Visa Policy, OJ L 231, 30.6.2021, pp. 159–706. 2 https://peka-program.gr/dimosieysi-odigoy-efarmogis-tis-drasis-anakainisi-katoikias/.
